appraisal_events.evidence: Hélas, d'aucune de ces personnes le mépris ne m'était aussi pénible que celui de M. de Stermaria.
appraisal_events.explanation: Among all the transient hotel notabilities whose opinion the narrator craves, M. de Stermaria's contempt is singled out as the most painful, marking a clear local snub of the narrator by him.

appraisal_events.evidence: un hasard mit tout d'un coup entre nos mains le moyen de nous donner à ma grand'mère et à moi... un prestige immédiat... excitant chez tous une curiosité et un respect auxquels il fut visible qu'échappait moins que personne M. de Stermaria... « La Marquise de Villeparisis »... cette dame apercevant ma grand'mère ne pouvait retenir un regard de joyeuse surprise.
appraisal_events.explanation: The director's public identification of the grandmother's acquaintance with the well-regarded Marquise de Villeparisis, and the marquise's own warm recognition of her, suddenly confer prestige on the grandmother (and, by extension, the narrator) before the whole hotel, notably including M. de Stermaria.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator is locally pained by being held in contempt by M. de Stermaria, whose regard he especially craves.
The narrator shares in the sudden prestige his grandmother gains through her connection to Mme de Villeparisis, since the passage frames the gain as benefiting both of them.
The grandmother is clearly elevated in the eyes of the whole hotel once her acquaintance with the respected Marquise de Villeparisis becomes visible.

ambiguities: It is unclear whether M. de Stermaria's being swept into the collective respect for the grandmother in the closing paragraph implies any real softening of the personal contempt he holds for the narrator, or merely reflects generalized deference to Mme de Villeparisis's circle; the two movements involving him are not explicitly connected by the text.
